sections.h2: Where is Sweetwater County, Wyoming, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Sweetwater County is in southwestern Wyoming, borders Colorado and Utah, and is the largest county in the state by area. Wikipedia gives the total as 10,491 square miles, with the Continental Divide running through it and most of the Great Divide Basin in its northeast quadrant.

Green River is the county seat and Rock Springs is the largest city. The county was created on December 17, 1867, as Carter County, and was renamed in 1869 for the Sweetwater River. South Pass City was the first seat, and the seat moved to Green River after 1873.

For a property owner, size is the point. The county has about 4 people per square mile, so a parcel can be a city lot in Rock Springs or a long way from anything, and both are handled by the same two courthouse offices in Green River.

sections.html:

sections.h2: What drives the Sweetwater County economy?
sections.html:
Trona and the soda ash made from it are the base of the Sweetwater County economy. The Wyoming Business Council's Southwest profile says the county has the largest natural trona reserves in the world and names WE Soda and Ciner as major employers.

The Green River article says soda ash mining employs over 2,000 people at five mines, and notes the 80 MW Sweetwater Solar project near the city.

Transport matters too. The same Business Council profile describes Interstate 80 as an east-west freight corridor and says Union Pacific runs mainline and spur rail to mines and plants. Southwest Wyoming Regional Airport in Rock Springs has daily service to Denver, and Western Wyoming College is in Rock Springs.

Steady industrial payrolls tend to support the local housing market, but they also mean a large share of the tax base sits in plants and mines, not houses.

sections.h2: How is a Sweetwater County house assessed and taxed?
sections.html:
The Sweetwater County Assessor values every taxable parcel as of January 1, and a house is taxed on 9.5 percent of that value. The Assessor's page says valuations follow Wyoming statutes and Department of Revenue guidelines, and that voters, commissioners, state limits and assessed values set the tax rates.

The tax is the assessed value multiplied by the mills. University of Wyoming Extension gives a range of 65 to 80 mills for residential property and a sample of a $100,000 home at 70 mills producing about $665.

  • Industrial property, including mineral processing, is assessed at 11.5 percent.
  • Minerals and mine products are assessed at 100 percent.
  • Other real and personal property, including homes, is assessed at 9.5 percent.

Those percentages come from the Wyoming Taxpayers Association. The Assessor does not bill or collect. The Treasurer does.

sections.h2: What exemptions and refunds apply in Sweetwater County?
sections.html:
Sweetwater County homeowners can have several reductions at once, and they appear at the bottom of the notice of value. The Green River Star reported in April 2025 that the 25 percent cut from Senate File 69 was applied automatically that year.

  • The veteran's exemption rose from $3,000 to $6,000 for tax year 2025, and veterans missing it on the notice were told to contact the assessor by May 26.
  • The long-term homeowners exemption is for owners age 65 who have paid Wyoming property taxes for 25 years, live in the home eight months a year, and bring ID showing a birthdate.
  • The Property Tax Refund Program pays up to half the median residential tax or 75 percent of the 2024 bill, whichever is less, and taxes must be paid in full before applying.

Later rules changed. A February 2026 report said owners needed to file an affidavit with the county assessor by March 1 that year. Call the Assessor at 307-872-3700 for the current process.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Sweetwater County valuation?
sections.html:
You have 30 days from the mailing date of the notice of value to contact the Assessor and make your case. SweetwaterNOW reported in 2024 that the window is 30 days from mailing, and Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 requires a written statement of why the assessment is incorrect.

Notices usually go out in the spring. The 2025 notices were due in mailboxes in the days after April 10, per the Green River Star, and the 2024 notices after April 17.

A short checklist helps:

  • Find your parcel's value and exemptions on the notice.
  • Collect recent sales of comparable Rock Springs or Green River homes.
  • Document condition problems with photos and bids.
  • Send your written statement before the 30 days end.

The same 2024 article said Sweetwater County had the lowest residential value change in Wyoming for tax year 2022 to 2023, at 8.52 percent against a statewide average of 17.91 percent.

sections.h2: What should a homeowner expect from the weather in Rock Springs and Green River?
sections.html:
The area is semi-arid and cold. Wikipedia reports average precipitation in Rock Springs of 10.45 inches a year and average snowfall of 31.3 inches, with measurable precipitation on about 61.7 days a year.

Little rain does not mean easy winters. Freezing cold at roughly 6,000 feet is hard on roofs, pipes and furnaces, and a vacant house can develop trouble fast. If you are carrying an inherited or empty property, keep the heat on and the roof checked while the tax bill sits unpaid.

sections.h2: When are Sweetwater County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Statements are mailed in September and can be paid in full by December 31 or in two halves, the first by November 10 and the second by May 10. The Treasurer's page says weekend and holiday due dates move to the next business day, and mailed payments must be postmarked by the due date.

Pay or view a statement online at itax.sweetwatercountywy.gov. Late interest, the May 11 delinquency date and the tax lien sale are covered earlier on this page.

Real property taxes are a lien on the house, so any unpaid balance will need to be settled when the property sells.

sections.h2: How do you sell a Sweetwater County house with taxes due?
sections.html:
Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer, then decide how to close. An unpaid balance can be paid from the sale proceeds at the title company, and a cash buyer can purchase the house as-is without repairs.

Offices to contact, all in the Green River courthouse at 80 W. Flaming Gorge Way:

  • Treasurer, Suite 139: 307-872-3720 (the website footer shows 307-872-3970, so confirm), taxes@sweetwatercountywy.gov
  • Assessor, Suite 122: 307-872-3700, assessor@sweetwatercountywy.gov
  • Rock Springs Assessor line: 307-922-5200

Call us at (424) 435-2326 if you want a written cash offer for a Sweetwater County house.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Sweetwater County, Wyoming?
faqs.a: The County Treasurer in Green River. The Assessor values property but does not set tax amounts or collect them.

faqs.q: How long do I have to question my Sweetwater County notice of value?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the date the notice was mailed. Wyoming Statute 39-13-109 calls for a written statement, so contact the Assessor at 307-872-3700 well before the window closes.

faqs.q: What is the residential assessment rate in Sweetwater County?
faqs.a: 9.5 percent of market value. Industrial property is assessed at 11.5 percent and mineral production at 100 percent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sweetwater County house if I owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance has to be paid or settled at closing, and the Treasurer can give you a payoff amount.

faqs.q: Which Sweetwater County city is the county seat?
faqs.a: Green River. Rock Springs is larger, with 23,526 people at the 2020 census against 11,825 in Green River.

faqs.q: Is there a veteran's exemption in Sweetwater County?
faqs.a: Yes. It rose from $3,000 to $6,000 for tax year 2025. A veteran who does not see it on the notice should contact the Assessor's office.
